[USER] User inquired about the reactions of big market teams to the increase in salaries for top free agents.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant stated it does not have access to current news or recent data but can provide a general idea based on historical data.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In the past, big market teams have generally been willing to pay top salaries for free agents to strengthen their rosters and increase their chances of winning championships.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some big market teams have become more cautious in their spending due to increased scrutiny on team spending and revenue sharing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Many teams are focusing on building through their farm systems and developing young talent rather than signing high-priced free agents.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some teams prefer to sign players to shorter, more flexible deals instead of long-term contracts worth hundreds of millions of dollars.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The reactions of big market teams to salary increases vary depending on the team's financial situation, priorities, and long-term goals.  
[USER] User requested examples of big market teams that have become more cautious in their spending on top free agents.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided examples:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. New York Yankees - historically big spenders, now focusing on developing young talent and staying under the luxury tax threshold.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Los Angeles Dodgers - previously big spenders, now more efficient in spending and building a strong team without breaking the bank on top free agents.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Boston Red Sox - became more cautious after winning the World Series in 2018, trading away high-priced players to get under the luxury tax threshold.  
[USER] User asked if the trend towards developing young talent instead of signing high-priced free agents will continue among big market teams in the future.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant stated that the trend is likely to continue due to:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Increased emphasis on analytics allowing teams to identify young players with potential.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. The luxury tax threshold making it difficult to sign multiple high-priced free agents without penalties.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Recognition that building a strong core of homegrown players can lead to sustained success.  
[USER] User inquired about the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the spending of big market teams in MLB.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant noted that the pandemic significantly impacted spending due to reduced revenue from no fans and TV deals.
